_comment: Notable callsigns for HamLookup. Types: person or special. Icons: ⭐ person, ⚓ ship, 🛸 space, 📻 radio org, 🕐 time station, ✈️ aviation, 🚀 military, 📡 inventor/pioneer, 👑 royalty, 🎭 entertainment, 🎵 music. Volume-mounted at /app/notable_callsigns.json.

NA1SS.name: International Space Station (ARISS)
NA1SS.note: Primary US callsign for ISS ham radio. Active since December 21, 2000 — first ARISS contact by ISS Expedition 1 Commander Bill Shepherd.

RS0ISS.name: International Space Station (Russian)
RS0ISS.note: Russian callsign for ISS amateur radio operations.

DL0ISS.name: International Space Station (German)
DL0ISS.note: German callsign for ISS amateur radio operations.

JY1.name: King Hussein of Jordan
JY1.note: One of the most celebrated ham operators in history. Held one of the rarest callsigns — JY1. Known for making contacts with ordinary hams worldwide. Silent key 1999.

JY2.name: Queen Noor of Jordan
JY2.note: Wife of King Hussein (JY1), licensed ham radio operator.

EA0JC.name: Juan Carlos I of Spain
EA0JC.note: Former King of Spain, passionate amateur radio operator.

HS1A.name: Bhumibol Adulyadej
HS1A.note: Longest-reigning monarch in Thai history, avid ham radio operator. Silent key 2016.

HS1D.name: Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn
HS1D.note: Thai crown princess, licensed amateur radio operator.

A41AA.name: Qaboos bin Said Al Said
A41AA.note: Sultan of Oman, licensed amateur radio operator. Silent key 2020.

9K2CS.name: Prince Yousuf Al-Sabah
9K2CS.note: Member of the Kuwaiti royal family, licensed amateur radio operator.

HZ1TA.name: Prince Talal bin Abdulaziz
HZ1TA.profession: Saudi Arabian Prince / UN Goodwill Ambassador
HZ1TA.note: Saudi prince and UN Goodwill Ambassador, licensed ham radio operator.

CN8MH.name: King Hassan II of Morocco
CN8MH.note: King of Morocco, licensed amateur radio operator. Silent key 1999.

3A0AG.name: Prince Albert II of Monaco
3A0AG.note: Ruling Prince of Monaco, licensed amateur radio operator.

K7UGA.name: Barry Goldwater
K7UGA.note: Five-term US Senator from Arizona, 1964 Republican presidential nominee. Licensed since the 1920s (also 6BPI, K3UIG). Founded MARS. Silent key 1998.

W6RIP.name: Ronald Reagan
W6RIP.note: 40th President of the United States, licensed amateur radio operator.

W5KPI.name: Gerald Ford
W5KPI.note: 38th President of the United States, licensed amateur radio operator.

I0FCG.name: Francesco Cossiga
I0FCG.note: Former President of Italy, licensed amateur radio operator. Silent key 2010.

VU2RG.name: Rajiv Gandhi
VU2RG.note: Prime Minister of India, licensed amateur radio operator. Assassinated 1991. Callsign now held by a memorial radio club.

LU1SM.name: Carlos Menem
LU1SM.note: Former President of Argentina, licensed amateur radio operator.

JI1KIT.name: Keizo Obuchi
JI1KIT.note: Prime Minister of Japan 1998-2000, licensed amateur radio operator. Silent key 2000.

YN1AS.name: Anastasio Somoza
YN1AS.note: Former President of Nicaragua, licensed amateur radio operator.

K2ZCZ.name: George Pataki
K2ZCZ.note: Former Governor of New York, licensed amateur radio operator.

W7EQI.name: Greg Walden
W7EQI.note: Former US Congressman from Oregon, licensed amateur radio operator.

K2USA.name: Hoyt Vandenberg
K2USA.profession: USAF Chief of Staff / CIA Director
K2USA.note: Second Director of the CIA and second Chief of Staff of the US Air Force, licensed amateur radio operator.

VU288PS.name: Rajiv Gandhi
VU288PS.note: Prime Minister of India, licensed amateur radio operator. Assassinated 1991.

WB6ACU.name: Joe Walsh
WB6ACU.note: Guitarist for the Eagles and The James Gang, Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inductee. Amateur Extra class licensee, very active ham operator.

W4CGP.name: Chet Atkins
W4CGP.note: Legendary country guitarist, RCA Records producer, Country Music Hall of Fame inductee. Also licensed as WA4CZD. Silent key 2001.

WA4CZD.name: Chet Atkins
WA4CZD.note: Legendary country guitarist, RCA Records producer, Country Music Hall of Fame inductee. Also licensed as W4CGP. Silent key 2001.

WB4KCG.name: Ronnie Milsap
WB4KCG.note: Grammy Award-winning country music singer, licensed amateur radio operator.

KD4WUJ.name: Patty Loveless
KD4WUJ.note: Grammy Award-winning country music singer, licensed amateur radio operator.

WD4SKT.name: Donnie Osmond
WD4SKT.note: Singer and actor, licensed amateur radio operator.

W2JOF.name: Cliff Richard
W2JOF.note: British pop singer, licensed amateur radio operator (US callsign).

K9EID.name: Bob Heil
K9EID.note: Legendary sound engineer for The Who, Grateful Dead, and The Eagles. Founder of Heil Sound microphones, major contributor to amateur radio audio technology.

W6UK.name: Alvino Rey
W6UK.note: Pioneer of the electric and steel guitar, big band leader. Licensed amateur radio operator.

KG4UYY.name: Lance Bass
KG4UYY.note: Member of pop group *NSYNC, licensed amateur radio operator. Also trained as a cosmonaut.

K6UXU.name: Tex Beneke
K6UXU.note: Saxophonist and singer with the Glenn Miller Orchestra, licensed amateur radio operator.

KB2GSD.name: Walter Cronkite
KB2GSD.note: Legendary CBS Evening News anchor, also licensed as K0MIR. Called the most trusted man in America. Silent key 2009.

K0MIR.name: Walter Cronkite
K0MIR.note: Legendary CBS Evening News anchor, also licensed as KB2GSD. Called the most trusted man in America. Silent key 2009.

W6OBB.name: Art Bell
W6OBB.profession: Radio Host / Coast to Coast AM Founder
W6OBB.note: Creator and host of Coast to Coast AM, the late-night paranormal radio program. Active ham operator. Silent key 2018.

W2IKAM.name: Al Roker
W2IKAM.note: NBC Today Show meteorologist and weather anchor, licensed amateur radio operator.

N6FUP.name: Jean Shepherd
N6FUP.note: Beloved radio storyteller and author, narrator of A Christmas Story. Long-time ham radio enthusiast.

KA6BJW.name: Marlon Brando
KA6BJW.note: Academy Award-winning actor (The Godfather, Apocalypse Now). Also operated as KE6PZH and FO5GJ from his private island Tetiaroa. Silent key 2004.

KE6PZH.name: Marlon Brando
KE6PZH.note: Academy Award-winning actor (The Godfather, Apocalypse Now). Also operated as KA6BJW and FO5GJ from his private island Tetiaroa. Silent key 2004.

FO5GJ.name: Marlon Brando
FO5GJ.note: Academy Award-winning actor. Operated from his private island Tetiaroa in French Polynesia. Silent key 2004.

KK6OTD.name: Tim Allen
KK6OTD.note: Actor known for Home Improvement and the Toy Story franchise, licensed amateur radio operator.

WA7BKG.name: Garry Shandling
WA7BKG.note: Stand-up comedian and actor, creator of The Larry Sanders Show, licensed amateur radio operator. Silent key 2016.

W6UJS.name: Cliff Arquette
W6UJS.note: Actor and comedian, creator of the Charley Weaver character on The Tonight Show and Hollywood Squares. Silent key 1974.

WA6FQA.name: Stu Gilliam
WA6FQA.note: Comedian and actor, licensed amateur radio operator.

N6KGC.name: Priscilla Presley
N6KGC.note: Actress and businesswoman, ex-wife of Elvis Presley, licensed amateur radio operator.

NY6YOS.name: Priscilla Presley
NY6YOS.note: Actress and businesswoman, ex-wife of Elvis Presley, licensed amateur radio operator.

KG6FZX.name: Patty Hearst
KG6FZX.note: Granddaughter of William Randolph Hearst, known for 1974 SLA kidnapping. Licensed amateur radio operator.

WV6VLY.name: Steve Wozniak
WV6VLY.note: Co-founder of Apple Computer with Steve Jobs. Credits ham radio as foundational to his interest in electronics and computing.

K6HIH.name: Howard Hughes
K6HIH.note: Billionaire aviator, engineer, film producer, and philanthropist, licensed amateur radio operator.

K6RHL.name: Stuart Hamblen
K6RHL.note: Country gospel singer, actor, and 1952 Prohibition Party presidential candidate. Licensed amateur radio operator.

K4ZVZ.name: Paul Tibbets
K4ZVZ.note: Pilot of the Enola Gay that dropped the first atomic bomb on Hiroshima, August 6, 1945. Silent key 2007.

W6AM.name: Don Wallace
W6AM.note: Legendary DXer who built a famous 92-acre rhombic antenna farm in Palos Verdes, CA. Worked all countries multiple times.

W6ZH.name: Herbert Hoover III
W6ZH.note: Grandson of President Herbert Hoover, former ARRL and IARU President.

W6NRM.name: Robert Weitbrecht
W6NRM.profession: Inventor of TTY for the Deaf
W6NRM.note: Physicist who invented the acoustic coupler teletypewriter (TTY) enabling deaf people to use the telephone. Silent key 1983.

W5LFL.name: Owen Garriott
W5LFL.note: First amateur radio operator to operate from space (STS-9, 1983). Pioneer of ARISS. His son Richard also operated from ISS. Silent key 2019.

KD5GSL.name: William Shepherd
KD5GSL.note: Commander of ISS Expedition 1, made the first ARISS contact from ISS on December 21, 2000.

KC5ZSX.name: Sally Ride
KC5ZSX.note: First American woman in space (1983), licensed amateur radio operator. Silent key 2012.

WA4SIR.name: Ron Parise
WA4SIR.note: NASA payload specialist, flew on STS-51-G and STS-35. Silent key 2008.

GB1MIR.name: Helen Sharman
GB1MIR.note: First Briton in space (Mir space station, 1991), licensed amateur radio operator.

7L2NJY.name: Mamoru Mohri
7L2NJY.note: First Japanese citizen to travel in space (STS-47, 1992). Also licensed as JI1KDG.

JI1KDG.name: Mamoru Mohri
JI1KDG.note: First Japanese citizen to travel in space (STS-47, 1992). Also licensed as 7L2NJY.

DP3MIR.name: Ulf Merbold
DP3MIR.note: First ESA astronaut to fly on a US Space Shuttle (STS-9, 1983).

N5VHO.name: Rusty Schweickart
N5VHO.note: Apollo 9 lunar module pilot (1969), performed first spacewalk of Apollo program.

K1JT.name: Joseph H. Taylor Jr.
K1JT.note: 1993 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovery of binary pulsars. Creator of WSJT suite including FT8, FT4, JT65 — digital modes that revolutionized weak-signal amateur radio communication.

W8JK.name: John Kraus
W8JK.note: Pioneering radio astronomer, inventor of the W8JK beam and helical antenna. Author of classic radio and antenna textbooks. Silent key 2004.

JA3FA.name: Tokuzo Inoue
JA3FA.note: Founder of ICOM Incorporated, one of the world's leading amateur radio equipment manufacturers.

JA1MP.name: Sako Hasegawa
JA1MP.note: Founder of Yaesu Musen (now Vertex Standard), one of the world's leading amateur radio equipment manufacturers. Silent key.

XE1GC.name: Guillermo Gonzalez Camarena
XE1GC.note: Mexican engineer who invented the trichromatic field-sequential color television system in 1940. Licensed ham radio operator. Silent key 1965.

W1AW.name: ARRL Headquarters Station (W1AW)
W1AW.note: Official station of the American Radio Relay League in Newington, CT. Named after ARRL co-founder Hiram Percy Maxim. Transmits code practice and bulletins daily.

GB2SM.name: Science Museum London
GB2SM.note: Permanent amateur radio station at the London Science Museum.

MGY.name: RMS Titanic (Historic Wireless Station)
MGY.note: Marconi wireless station aboard the RMS Titanic. On April 14-15, 1912, operators Jack Phillips and Harold Bride transmitted the historic CQD and SOS distress signals during the sinking. One of the most famous radio events in history.

NSS.name: Annapolis Naval Radio Station (Historic)
NSS.note: Massive US Navy communication station active from WWI through the Cold War. Transmitted orders to naval vessels worldwide.

WSM.name: WSM — Grand Ole Opry Station
WSM.note: Clear-channel AM station (650 kHz) in Nashville, TN, home of the Grand Ole Opry. Instrumental in popularizing country music nationwide since 1925.

KDKA.name: KDKA — World's First Commercial Radio Station
KDKA.note: The world's first commercially licensed radio station, operated by Westinghouse Electric in Pittsburgh, PA. First broadcast November 2, 1920 covering the Harding-Cox presidential election results.

WWV.name: NIST Time Signal Station WWV
WWV.note: NIST official time and frequency standard in Fort Collins, CO. Transmits on 2.5, 5, 10, 15, 20 MHz continuously since 1923.

WWVH.name: NIST Time Signal Station WWVH
WWVH.note: NIST official time and frequency station in Kauai, HI. Female voice announcer distinguishes it from WWV. Transmits on 2.5, 5, 10, 15 MHz.

WWVB.name: NIST Time Signal Station WWVB
WWVB.note: NIST 60 kHz time signal in Fort Collins, CO. Used to synchronize atomic clocks and radio-controlled clocks across North America.

CHU.name: NRC Time Signal Station CHU
CHU.note: Canadian time signal station operated by the National Research Council in Ottawa. Transmits on 3.33, 7.85, 14.67 MHz.

WW2CV.name: USS Intrepid (Museum Ship)
WW2CV.note: WWII Essex-class aircraft carrier museum in New York City. Apollo 11 recovery ship. Grid: FN20gb.

NJ2BB.name: USS New Jersey (Museum Ship)
NJ2BB.note: Iowa-class battleship museum in Camden, NJ. Most decorated battleship in US Navy history. Grid: FM29jw.

NI4BK.name: USS North Carolina (Museum Ship)
NI4BK.note: WWII battleship museum in Wilmington, NC. First US battleship completed during WWII. Grid: FM04ff.

N4WIS.name: USS Wisconsin (Museum Ship)
N4WIS.note: Iowa-class battleship museum in Norfolk, VA. Last battleship built by the US Navy. Grid: FM16ts.

N2USS.name: USS Slater (Museum Ship)
N2USS.note: WWII destroyer escort museum in Albany, NY. Only restored destroyer escort afloat in the US. Grid: FN32dq.

WA4USN.name: USS Yorktown (Museum Ship)
WA4USN.note: WWII Essex-class carrier museum in Mount Pleasant, SC. Earned 11 battle stars. Grid: FM02os.

NE1PL.name: USS Massachusetts (Museum Ship)
NE1PL.note: WWII battleship museum in Fall River, MA. Fired first and last US naval shots in European theater. Grid: FN41or.

NJ4I.name: USS Torsk (Museum Ship)
NJ4I.note: WWII submarine museum in Baltimore, MD. Sank last Japanese combatant vessels of WWII. Grid: FM19hf.

KH6BB.name: USS Missouri (Museum Ship)
KH6BB.note: Iowa-class battleship museum at Pearl Harbor, HI. Site of Japanese surrender September 2, 1945. Grid: BL11cj. POTA: US-4428.

NE6PP.name: USS Iowa (Museum Ship)
NE6PP.note: Iowa-class battleship museum in Los Angeles, CA. Served in WWII, Korea, and Cold War. Grid: DM03to.

NI6IW.name: USS Midway (Museum Ship)
NI6IW.note: Aircraft carrier museum in San Diego, CA. Longest-serving US carrier of the 20th century (1945-1992). Grid: DM12jw.

NB6GC.name: USS Hornet (Museum Ship)
NB6GC.note: WWII Essex-class carrier museum in Alameda, CA. Recovery ship for Apollo 11 and Apollo 12. Grid: CM87ut.

NJ6VT.name: USS Pampanito (Museum Ship)
NJ6VT.note: WWII submarine museum in San Francisco, CA. Sank 6 Japanese ships. Grid: CM87uu. POTA: US-0134.

NS7DD.name: USS Turner Joy (Museum Ship)
NS7DD.note: Destroyer museum in Bremerton, WA. Involved in the Gulf of Tonkin incident (1964). Grid: CN87tm.

W5KID.name: USS Kidd (Museum Ship)
W5KID.note: WWII destroyer museum in Baton Rouge, LA. Known as The Pirate of the Pacific. Grid: EM30dl.

K5XOM.name: USS Alabama (Museum Ship)
K5XOM.note: WWII battleship museum in Mobile, AL. Earned 9 battle stars. Grid: EM50eq.

W5R.name: USS Razorback (Museum Ship)
W5R.note: WWII submarine museum in North Little Rock, AR. Served in both US and Turkish navies. Grid: EM34tr.

WW2SUB.name: USS Batfish (Museum Ship)
WW2SUB.note: WWII Balao-class submarine museum in Muskogee, OK. Sank three Japanese submarines in 76 hours, a record. Also operated as WW2SUB for USS Cavalla.

WW2R.name: USS Stewart (Museum Ship)
WW2R.note: WWII destroyer escort museum in Galveston, TX. Grid: EL29gh.

GB2BP.name: HMS Belfast (Museum Ship)
GB2BP.note: WWII light cruiser museum on the Thames in London. Participated in D-Day bombardment. Grid: IO91om. IOTA: EU-120.

VA3WWV.name: HMCS Haida (Museum Ship)
VA3WWV.note: WWII destroyer museum in Hamilton, ON, Canada. Most decorated warship in Canadian naval history. Grid: FN03ch. POTA: CA-0182.

CY3S.name: HMCS Sackville (Museum Ship)
CY3S.note: WWII corvette museum in Halifax, NS, Canada. Only surviving Canadian WWII corvette. Grid: FN84dq.

VK2VMP.name: HMAS Vampire (Museum Ship)
VK2VMP.note: Destroyer museum at the Australian National Maritime Museum, Sydney. Grid: QF56id.

VK6SUB.name: HMAS Ovens (Museum Ship)
VK6SUB.note: Oberon-class submarine museum in Fremantle, Western Australia. Grid: OF78ee.

DL0DMB.name: U-995 Submarine Museum
DL0DMB.note: WWII Type VIIC U-boat museum in Laboe, Germany. Only surviving Type VIIC submarine. Grid: JO54al.

R1LK.name: Krasin Icebreaker Museum
R1LK.note: Historic steam-powered icebreaker museum in St. Petersburg, Russia. Grid: KO59cw.

SZ1AB.name: HS Georgios Averof (Museum Ship)
SZ1AB.note: Historic armored cruiser museum in Athens, Greece. Only surviving pre-dreadnought warship in the world. Grid: KM17ux.

W3E.name: Smithsonian Udvar-Hazy Aerospace Center
W3E.note: National Air and Space Museum annex near Dulles Airport, Chantilly, VA. Houses Space Shuttle Discovery and the Enola Gay. Grid: FM18lw.

K3S.name: Nuclear Ship Savannah ARC
K3S.note: Amateur Radio Club aboard the NS Savannah, the world's first nuclear-powered merchant ship, now a museum ship in Baltimore, MD.

W7GV.name: Titan Missile Museum
W7GV.note: Only remaining intact Titan II ICBM launch site in Green Valley, AZ. National Historic Landmark. Grid: DM41ov.

W0MA.name: National Museum of Transportation
W0MA.note: Large transportation museum in St. Louis, MO featuring locomotives, cars, and aircraft. Grid: EM48ho.

K0MAN.name: Strategic Air Command & Aerospace Museum
K0MAN.note: Aviation and space museum in Ashland, NE featuring B-52, SR-71, and other historic aircraft. Grid: EN11cb.

VE9BELL.name: Alexander Graham Bell Museum
VE9BELL.note: Museum dedicated to Bell's later life and inventions in Baddeck, NS, Canada. Grid: FN86ec. POTA: CA-0010. IOTA: NA-010.

IY4FGM.name: Guglielmo Marconi Historical Museum
IY4FGM.note: Museum at Marconi's birthplace in Pontecchio Marconi, Italy where he conducted early radio experiments. Grid: JN54qk.

K2AMH.name: Robert Moog
K2AMH.note: Engineer and inventor who created the Moog synthesizer, revolutionizing electronic music. Silent key 2005.

K2GL.name: Hazard Reeves
K2GL.note: Inventor of the modern stereo sound system used in theaters and broadcasting. Silent key 1986.

W2BML.name: Harold Beverage
W2BML.note: Radio engineer who invented the Beverage antenna (wave antenna) in 1921, still widely used today. Silent key 1993.

K2ORS.name: Jean Shepherd
K2ORS.note: Beloved radio storyteller, humorist, and author. Narrator and writer of A Christmas Story. Long-time ham radio enthusiast. Silent key 1999.

KB1NXP.name: John Baldacci
KB1NXP.note: Former Governor of Maine, licensed amateur radio operator.

K4LIB.name: Arthur Godfrey
K4LIB.note: Legendary radio and TV personality, one of the most powerful figures in American broadcasting in the 1950s. Licensed amateur radio operator. Silent key 1983.

K4EB.name: Larry Junstrom
K4EB.note: Bass player for 38 Special and founding member of Lynyrd Skynyrd. Licensed amateur radio operator. Silent key 2019.

KF5BOX.name: Doug Wheelock
KF5BOX.note: Commander of ISS Expedition 25, conducted ARISS school contacts from the station. Active ham operator.

K5CSG.name: Peggy Sue Gerron
K5CSG.profession: Inspiration for Buddy Holly's Peggy Sue
K5CSG.note: The real Peggy Sue behind Buddy Holly's 1957 hit song, licensed amateur radio operator.

N5QWL.name: Jay Apt
N5QWL.note: NASA astronaut who flew on four Space Shuttle missions, conducted ham radio contacts from space. Professor at Carnegie Mellon University.

N5RAX.name: Linda Godwin
N5RAX.note: NASA astronaut who flew on four Space Shuttle missions including a docking with Mir. Licensed amateur radio operator.

W6EZV.name: Curtis LeMay
W6EZV.note: USAF General, Strategic Air Command chief, and 1968 American Independent Party vice-presidential candidate with George Wallace. Licensed amateur radio operator. Silent key 1990.

KA6HVK.name: Burl Ives
KA6HVK.note: Oscar-winning actor and folk singer, known for A Holly Jolly Christmas and Cat on a Hot Tin Roof. Licensed amateur radio operator. Silent key 1995.

N6KGB.name: Stewart Granger
N6KGB.note: British-American film actor known for adventure films of the 1950s, licensed amateur radio operator. Silent key 1993.

KB6LQS.name: Dick Rutan
KB6LQS.note: Pilot who with Jeana Yeager completed the first nonstop unrefueled circumnavigation of the globe (Voyager, 1986). Licensed amateur radio operator.

WB6RER.name: Andy Devine
WB6RER.note: Western film actor known for his distinctive gravelly voice, appeared in hundreds of films. Licensed amateur radio operator. Silent key 1977.

WB4APR.name: Bob Bruninga
WB4APR.note: US Naval Academy engineer who invented APRS (Automatic Packet Reporting System) in 1992 — used worldwide for real-time digital position and communications. Silent key 2022.

9DRV.name: David Packard
9DRV.note: Co-founded Hewlett-Packard with Bill Hewlett in a Palo Alto garage in 1939. Deputy Secretary of Defense 1969-1971. Licensed amateur radio operator. Silent key 1996.

W0CXX.name: Art Collins
W0CXX.note: Founded Collins Radio Company in 1933, manufacturer of legendary amateur and military radio equipment. Silent key 1987.

RV3DW.name: Sergei Avdeyev
RV3DW.note: Russian cosmonaut who holds the record for cumulative time in space (747 days across three missions to Mir space station). Licensed amateur radio operator.

DG1KIM.name: Ulrich Walter
DG1KIM.note: German astronaut who flew on STS-55 (Spacelab D-2, 1993). Now professor of astronautics at TU Munich. Licensed amateur radio operator.

9N1MM.name: Father Marshall Moran
9N1MM.note: Jesuit priest and educator who spent decades in Nepal, licensed amateur radio operator. Used radio to connect Nepal with the outside world.

NS3T.name: Jamie Dupree
NS3T.note: Cox Media Group Washington DC correspondent, veteran Capitol Hill reporter, licensed amateur radio operator.

K6DUE.name: Roy Neal
K6DUE.note: NBC News correspondent and space program reporter, licensed amateur radio operator. Active ARRL member. Silent key 2014.

W6APW.name: Herbert Hoover III
W6APW.note: Herbert Pete Hoover III, grandson of President Herbert Hoover, major AMSAT fundraiser and ARRL volunteer.

KA6UXR.name: Alexander Comfort
KA6UXR.note: British physician and author, best known for writing The Joy of Sex (1972). Licensed amateur radio operator.

W6FZZ.name: Samuel F.B. Morse III
W6FZZ.note: Great-grandson of Samuel F.B. Morse, inventor of Morse code and the telegraph. Licensed amateur radio operator.

KI6M.name: Stu Gilliam
KI6M.note: Comedian and actor. Also licensed as WA6FQA.

KD6OY.name: Garry Shandling
KD6OY.note: Stand-up comedian and actor, creator of The Larry Sanders Show. Also licensed as WA7BKG. Silent key 2016.

NK7U.name: Joe Rudi
NK7U.note: Oakland Athletics outfielder, three-time World Series champion (1972-74), three-time Gold Glove winner. Licensed amateur radio operator.

W0FQY.name: Carl Mosley
W0FQY.note: Founded Mosley Electronics, manufacturer of amateur radio antennas. Pioneer in beam antenna design.

W8OK.name: Frank Schwab
W8OK.note: Legendary organizer of Hamvention, the world's largest amateur radio gathering in Dayton, Ohio. Known as Mr. Hamvention.

WA5AVA.name: Clyde Clifford
WA5AVA.note: Radio personality who hosted the legendary Beaker Street late-night rock program on KAAY Little Rock in the late 1960s-70s. Licensed amateur radio operator.

N4KET.name: David French
N4KET.note: CNN news anchor, licensed amateur radio operator.

KA7EVD.name: Donnie Osmond
KA7EVD.note: Singer and actor, formerly licensed as KA7EVD (now expired). License held by WD4SKT is a different person.

W6BNB.name: Robert Shrader
W6BNB.note: Author of Electronic Communications, the definitive textbook used in electronics and radio education for decades.

8CR.name: Powell Crosley Jr.
8CR.note: Founded WLW (the Nation's Station) in Cincinnati, manufactured Crosley radios and appliances, owned the Cincinnati Reds. Pioneer of clear-channel broadcasting. Silent key 1961.

TI2DR.name: David Ruben
TI2DR.note: Physician and author, best known for Everything You Always Wanted to Know About Sex (1969). Licensed amateur radio operator.

ZK1AN.name: Sir Thomas Davis
ZK1AN.note: Former Premier of the Cook Islands, physician, and author. Licensed amateur radio operator.

W4LAA.name: Paul Kangas
W4LAA.note: Co-anchor of PBS Nightly Business Report for over 30 years. Licensed amateur radio operator. Silent key 2011.

WD4LZC.name: Larnell Harris
WD4LZC.note: Country and Christian music recording artist, licensed amateur radio operator.

K3SAV.name: NS Savannah (Museum Ship)
K3SAV.note: First nuclear-powered merchant ship in the world. Museum ship at the Port of Baltimore, MD. Operated 1962-1972. National Historic Landmark.

W1SSB.name: USS Salem (Museum Ship)
W1SSB.note: Heavy cruiser museum ship in Quincy, MA. Last all-gun heavy cruiser built. Now the United States Naval Shipbuilding Museum.

N3BBQ.name: USS Constellation (Museum Ship)
N3BBQ.note: Sloop-of-war museum ship in Baltimore, MD. Last all-sail warship designed and built by the US Navy (1854).

W1GSL.name: USS Cassin Young (Museum Ship)
W1GSL.note: WWII Fletcher-class destroyer museum at the Boston National Historical Park, MA. POTA eligible.

K5TBG.name: USS Texas (Museum Ship)
K5TBG.note: Dreadnought battleship museum ship, the last surviving WWI-era dreadnought. Undergoing restoration. Texas City, TX.

N0ESP.name: USS South Dakota (Memorial)
N0ESP.note: WWII battleship memorial in Sioux Falls, SD. The ship itself was scrapped but the memorial preserves her history. Also activated as N0EBC.

K8GUN.name: USS Cod (Museum Ship)
K8GUN.note: WWII Gato-class submarine museum in Cleveland, OH. Only submarine museum ship with all original equipment intact.

W3EAX.name: USS Constellation (Frigate, Museum)
W3EAX.note: Frigate museum at the Inner Harbor, Baltimore, MD.

VE2CSL.name: Submarine Onondaga (Museum Ship)
VE2CSL.note: Oberon-class submarine museum at Musée Maritime de la Pointe-au-Père, Rimouski, QC, Canada. Only submarine museum in Eastern Canada.

W1ZE.name: Irving Vermilya
W1ZE.profession: First Licensed Radio Amateur in the US
W1ZE.note: Holder of the first amateur radio license issued in the United States.

W2SGG.name: Robert Cusumano
W2SGG.note: Co-inventor of the printed circuit board, foundational technology for all modern electronics. Licensed amateur radio operator.

NE2Q.name: Jay Kolinsky
NE2Q.note: Inventor of the electronic siren used in emergency vehicles. Licensed amateur radio operator.

W0WY.name: Yuri Gagarin
W0WY.profession: First Human in Space / Soviet Cosmonaut
W0WY.note: First human to journey into outer space (April 12, 1961). Licensed amateur radio operator. Silent key 1968.

UA1LO.name: Yuri Gagarin
UA1LO.profession: First Human in Space / Soviet Cosmonaut
UA1LO.note: First human to journey into outer space (April 12, 1961). Licensed amateur radio operator under Soviet callsign. Silent key 1968.

W5LEX.name: USS Lexington (Museum Ship)
W5LEX.note: Essex-class aircraft carrier museum in Corpus Christi, TX. Known as 'The Blue Ghost'. Served WWII through Cold War.

NI6BB.name: USS Iowa (Museum Ship)
NI6BB.note: Iowa-class battleship museum in San Pedro (Los Angeles), CA. Also operated as NE6PP.

NE4MW.name: USS Alabama (Museum Ship)
NE4MW.note: WWII South Dakota-class battleship museum in Mobile, AL. Also operated as K5XOM.

NA5DV.name: USS Texas (Museum Ship)
NA5DV.note: WWI-era dreadnought battleship museum in Baytown, TX. Last surviving WWI dreadnought battleship. Recently restored.

WW2OK.name: USS Oklahoma Mast Memorial
WW2OK.note: Memorial to USS Oklahoma (battleship sunk at Pearl Harbor) in Muskogee, OK.

W4BSF.name: USS Tennessee Museum
W4BSF.note: Battleship museum memorial in Oneida, TN. Special event station.

K8E.name: SS Col. James M. Schoonmaker (Museum Ship)
K8E.note: Historic Great Lakes bulk carrier museum in Toledo, OH. Largest ship on the Great Lakes when built (1911).

DL0MCM.name: MV Dresden (Museum Ship)
DL0MCM.note: Cargo ship museum in Rostock, Germany.

DL0MFH.name: MV Cap San Diego (Museum Ship)
DL0MFH.note: General cargo ship museum in Hamburg, Germany. One of the largest preserved cargo ships in the world.

KN4RAM.name: CSS Neuse (Museum Ship)
KN4RAM.note: Civil War Confederate ironclad gunboat museum in Kinston, NC. One of only two surviving Confederate ironclads.

NE6JP.name: USS Potomac (Museum Ship)
NE6JP.note: USCG Cutter / Presidential Yacht used by FDR, known as the Floating White House. Museum in Oakland, CA.

N1SLM.name: USS Salem (Museum Ship)
N1SLM.note: Heavy cruiser museum in Quincy, MA. Last all-gun heavy cruiser built by the US Navy. Also operated as W1SSB.

W2PE.name: USS Little Rock (Museum Ship)
W2PE.note: CLG-4 guided missile cruiser museum in Buffalo, NY. Last warship commissioned by the US Navy in WWII.

WA3BAT.name: USS Olympia (Museum Ship)
WA3BAT.note: Protected cruiser museum in Philadelphia, PA. Oldest steel-hulled warship still afloat. Carried Admiral Dewey at Battle of Manila Bay (1898).

WW2IND.name: USS Indianapolis CA-35 Memorial
WW2IND.note: Memorial to the heavy cruiser sunk by Japanese submarine in 1945 after delivering atomic bomb components. Indianapolis, IN.

WJ4DD.name: USS Orleck (Museum Ship)
WJ4DD.note: WWII Gearing-class destroyer museum in Jacksonville, FL.

W2S.name: USS The Sullivans (Museum Ship)
W2S.note: WWII destroyer museum in Buffalo, NY. Named after the five Sullivan brothers killed in WWII. Inspired the movie Saving Private Ryan.

VE0NV.name: HMCS Haida (Museum Ship)
VE0NV.note: WWII Tribal-class destroyer museum in Hamilton, ON, Canada. Also operated as VA3WWV.

NT4HI.name: USS Laffey (Museum Ship)
NT4HI.note: WWII Sumner-class destroyer museum in Charleston, SC. Survived being hit by 5 kamikazes and 3 bombs on April 16, 1945. Known as The Ship That Would Not Die.

WW2DD.name: USS Cassin Young (Museum Ship)
WW2DD.note: WWII Fletcher-class destroyer museum at Boston National Historical Park, MA. Also operated as W1GSL.

WW2DEM.name: USS Slater (Museum Ship)
WW2DEM.note: WWII Edsall-class destroyer escort museum in Albany, NY. Also operated as N2USS.

N5FKP.name: USS Stewart / USS Cavalla (Museum Ships)
N5FKP.note: WWII destroyer escort and submarine museums in Galveston, TX. Seawolf Park.

VE0CNM.name: HMCS Sackville (Museum Ship)
VE0CNM.note: WWII Flower-class corvette museum in Halifax, NS, Canada. Also operated as CY3S.

K5BS.name: SS Grandcamp Memorial
K5BS.note: Memorial to the French Liberty Ship whose cargo explosion caused the Texas City Disaster (1947), deadliest industrial accident in US history. Texas City, TX.

WA5DTK.name: USS Houston Memorial
WA5DTK.note: Memorial to the heavy cruiser sunk in the Battle of Sunda Strait (1942). Houston, TX.

W6RO.name: RMS Queen Mary (Museum Ship)
W6RO.note: Famous ocean liner museum in Long Beach, CA. Served as a luxury liner and WWII troopship. Now a hotel and museum.

K6JOB.name: SS Jeremiah O'Brien (Museum Ship)
K6JOB.note: WWII Liberty ship museum in San Francisco, CA. One of only two operational Liberty ships remaining. Participated in D-Day.

K8JWB.name: SS John W. Brown (Museum Ship)
K8JWB.note: WWII Liberty ship museum in Baltimore, MD. One of only two operational Liberty ships remaining.

W2AQ.name: Lightship Ambrose (Museum Ship)
W2AQ.note: Historic lightship museum on the East River in New York City. Guided ships into New York Harbor.

NM8GS.name: Lightship Huron (Museum Ship)
NM8GS.note: Historic Great Lakes lightship museum in Port Huron, MI. Last remaining Great Lakes lightship.

WW2LST.name: USS LST-325 (Museum Ship)
WW2LST.note: WWII tank landing ship museum in Evansville, IN. One of only two surviving WWII LSTs. Participated in D-Day.

N8LST.name: LST-393 (Museum Ship)
N8LST.note: WWII tank landing ship museum in Muskegon, MI. One of only two surviving WWII LSTs.

W1WCC.name: Chatham Radio / WCC Station
W1WCC.note: Historic maritime radio station in Chatham, MA. Operated as WCC, one of the most important maritime communication stations on the US East Coast.

K6KPH.name: Maritime Radio Historical Society / KPH
K6KPH.note: Restored historic RCA maritime radio station at Point Reyes Station, CA. KPH was one of the most important ship-to-shore radio stations in the world.

NB9QV.name: USS Cobia (Museum Ship)
NB9QV.note: WWII Gato-class submarine museum in Manitowoc, WI. Identical to USS Silversides. Built at the Manitowoc Shipbuilding Company.

N1S.name: USS Nautilus (Museum Ship)
N1S.note: World's first nuclear-powered submarine museum in Groton, CT. First vessel to complete a submerged transit of the North Pole (1958). National Historic Landmark.

N5R.name: USS Razorback (Museum Ship)
N5R.note: WWII submarine museum in North Little Rock, AR. Also operated as W5R.

K4DSR.name: USS Drum (Museum Ship)
K4DSR.note: WWII Tambor-class submarine museum in Mobile, AL. First US submarine to sink an enemy vessel in WWII. Earned 12 war patrol battle stars.

NM1JY.name: USS Albacore (Museum Ship)
NM1JY.note: Experimental submarine museum in Portsmouth, NH. Pioneered the teardrop hull design used by all modern submarines.

W2C.name: USS Croaker (Museum Ship)
W2C.note: WWII Gato-class submarine museum in Buffalo, NY. Sank the Japanese cruiser Nagara.

W8COD.name: USS Cod (Museum Ship)
W8COD.note: WWII Gato-class submarine museum in Cleveland, OH. Only submarine museum with all original equipment intact. Also operated as K8GUN.

VA2GNQ.name: Submarine Onondaga (Museum Ship)
VA2GNQ.note: Oberon-class submarine museum at Musée Maritime de la Pointe-au-Père, Rimouski, QC, Canada. Only submarine museum in Eastern Canada. Also operated as VE2CSL.

W7SUB.name: USS Blueback (Museum Ship)
W7SUB.note: Last non-nuclear attack submarine in US Navy service. Museum at Oregon Museum of Science and Industry, Portland, OR. Appeared in The Hunt for Red October.

N8SUB.name: USS Silversides (Museum Ship)
N8SUB.note: WWII Gato-class submarine museum in Muskegon, MI. Third-highest scoring US submarine of WWII with 23 ships sunk.

NK3ST.name: USS Torsk (Museum Ship)
NK3ST.note: WWII submarine museum in Baltimore, MD. Also operated as NJ4I. Sank the last Japanese combatant vessels of WWII.

N4HLH.name: H.L. Hunley (Museum Ship)
N4HLH.note: Civil War Confederate submarine in conservation in Charleston, SC. First submarine to sink an enemy warship (1864). Recently conserved after being raised in 2000.

W1WQM.name: USS Thresher Memorial
W1WQM.note: Memorial to USS Thresher (SSN-593) lost with all 129 crew in 1963, the worst submarine disaster in US history. Kittery, ME.

N7P.name: USS Parche Memorial
N7P.note: Memorial to USS Parche (SS-384), most decorated US submarine of WWII. Bremerton, WA.

W4AVM.name: SS American Victory (Museum Ship)
W4AVM.note: WWII Victory Ship museum in Tampa, FL. One of only four operational Victory Ships remaining.

K6YVM.name: Red Oak Victory (Museum Ship)
K6YVM.note: WWII Victory Ship museum in Richmond, CA. Named for Red Oak, Iowa. One of only four operational Victory Ships remaining.

IY4PRC.name: Elettra — Marconi's Yacht
IY4PRC.note: Replica of Guglielmo Marconi's famous research yacht Elettra, housed at Pontecchio Marconi, Italy. Marconi conducted groundbreaking radio experiments aboard the original.

W8AGB.name: USCGC Mackinaw WAGB-83 (Museum Ship)
W8AGB.note: Historic Coast Guard icebreaker museum in Mackinaw City, MI. Served the Great Lakes 1944-2006. Maritime Museum.

8S0HRA.name: SS Sankt Erik (Museum Ship)
8S0HRA.note: Historic Swedish icebreaker museum in Stockholm, Sweden.

PA40AC.name: HNLMS Abraham Crijnssen (Museum Ship)
PA40AC.note: WWII Dutch minesweeper museum in Den Helder, Netherlands. Famous for disguising itself as a jungle island to escape Japanese forces in 1942.

PI4HAL.name: SS Rotterdam (Museum Ship)
PI4HAL.note: Former Holland America Line ocean liner museum in Rotterdam, Netherlands.

TM2FLO.name: Flore (Museum Submarine)
TM2FLO.note: French Navy Daphné-class submarine museum in Lorient, France.

II1NS.name: Nazario Sauro (Museum Submarine)
II1NS.note: Italian Navy submarine museum in Genoa, Italy.

ZL2KS.name: Edwin Fox (Museum Ship)
ZL2KS.note: Historic British merchant vessel museum in Picton, New Zealand. One of the oldest surviving merchant ships in the world (1853).

W6N.name: WWII Base End Station
W6N.note: Restored WWII Army coastal defense radio/fire control station in San Diego, CA. Used to triangulate enemy ship positions.

N0K.name: USS Pueblo Memorial
N0K.note: Memorial to USS Pueblo (AGER-2), intelligence ship captured by North Korea in 1968. Still held by North Korea — only US Navy ship currently in enemy hands. Pueblo, CO.

N5H.name: USS Hoga YT-146 (Museum Ship)
N5H.note: WWII harbor tug that fought fires at Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941. Museum in North Little Rock, AR. Only Pearl Harbor attack vessel still afloat.

W4NNK.name: Claud W. Somers (Museum Skipjack)
W4NNK.note: Chesapeake Bay skipjack oyster dredger museum in Reedville, VA.

W1E.name: Evelina M. Goulart (Museum Schooner)
W1E.note: Historic fishing schooner museum in Essex, MA. Built 1927, represents the Essex-built fishing vessel tradition.

VA3VGC.name: SS Keewatin (Museum Ship)
VA3VGC.note: Edwardian-era passenger steamship museum in Kingston, ON, Canada. Last surviving steamship from the original CPR Great Lakes fleet (1907).

JS1YMG.name: JAXA SLIM Lunar Lander
JS1YMG.note: First amateur radio station on the Moon. Japan's Smart Lander for Investigating Moon (SLIM) transmitted on 437.410 MHz from the lunar surface, January 2024.

KD5FMU.name: Ham Radio Crusader
KD5FMU.note: Freddie Mac McGuire — ham radio YouTuber and AllStarLink community educator. YouTube: Ham Radio Crusader. Based in Henryetta, Oklahoma.

N0WRL.name: James Cribbs
N0WRL.profession: Founder, World Radio League & Ham Radio Prep
N0WRL.note: Founded Ham Radio Prep (2018) and World Radio League (2023). Electrical/Biomedical Engineering, Vanderbilt. Ham radio logging and contesting platform developer.

KK6OTD.name: Tim Allen
KK6OTD.note: Actor and comedian, known for Home Improvement and Toy Story. Licensed amateur radio operator. Legal name Timothy Dick.
